event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The 2022-02-17 Form 10-K squarely positions COVID-19 as a RECENT (≤2-year) external shock that is already eroding Johnson & Johnson’s performance and could further destabilise every major operational pillar—manufacturing, supply chain, labour arrangements, product demand and even R&D/clinical trials.  Most disclosures sit in the Risk-Factors section, so the language is partly cautionary, yet the filing also admits CURRENT, tangible damage: lower sales, reduced product usage and forced changes such as large-scale remote-work.  At the same time, management outlines only high-level mitigations (“business-continuity plans”), then immediately concedes those plans may prove insufficient.  No dollar figures are supplied, but the breadth of functions cited and the admission of ongoing uncertainty elevate the severity.  Under the Time-Decay Principle, COVID-19 is well inside the 0-3-year “recent” window, so snippet scores can legitimately reach the upper band (7-10) when multiple critical functions or realised impacts are described.  Generic or mitigated statements still earn lower marks, but none are forced to zero because the pandemic predates the filing.  The resulting evidence pattern shows a spectrum from moderate warnings (scores 2-4) to strong, multi-faceted, realised-impact statements (scores 6-8).

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has adversely impacted certain aspects of the Company’s business and could cause disruptions or future impact to the Company’s business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Explicitly states that COVID-19 has already caused adverse impacts (realised harm).
Covers broad areas: business operations, results and financial condition.
Lacks quantitative detail.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct admission of realised harm across multiple dimensions but unquantified; scored mid-high at 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We are subject to risks associated with global health crises, epidemics and pandemics, including the global outbreak of coronavirus and its variants (COVID-19).

components.reason: Identifies exposure to global pandemics explicitly referencing COVID-19 and variants.
Generic statement of exposure without detailing impact or magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges broad exposure but provides no impact detail; low-moderate risk recognised.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has adversely impacted, and is expected to continue to adversely impact, certain aspects of the Company’s business, results of operations and financial condition, including lower sales and reduced customer demand and usage of certain of our products.

components.reason: States both current and continuing adverse impacts.
Specifies concrete effects: lower sales and reduced demand/usage.
Still lacks dollars or percentages.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realised and ongoing demand/sales damage yields a solid severity score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The spread of COVID-19 has caused the Company to modify its business practices (including instituting remote work for many of the Company’s employees), and the Company may take further actions as may be required by government authorities or as the Company determines are in the best interests of our patients, customers, employees and business partners.

components.reason: Details operational disruption—forced remote-work transition.
Highlights possibility of additional mandated actions (future uncertainty).
Implies some control by noting company-determined actions (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows operational change but with some self-managed mitigation; modest score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: The Company continues to monitor the situation and while we have robust business continuity plans in place across our global supply chain network to help mitigate the impact of COVID-19, these efforts may not completely prevent our business from being adversely affected and future impacts remain uncertain.

components.reason: Admits uncertainty and possible insufficiency of mitigation measures.
References global supply-chain exposure.
Presence of ‘robust business continuity plans’ is a mitigating factor.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Supply-chain focus plus doubt over mitigation elevates risk despite stated plans; score 4.

evidence_list.snippet: While the U.S. and other countries have begun or will begin to reopen their economies, the extent to which COVID-19 will impact the Company’s future operations will depend on many factors which cannot be predicted with confidence, including the duration of the outbreak and impact of variants.

components.reason: Highlights uncontrollable, unpredictable factors (duration, variants).
Forward-looking uncertainty without specifics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pure uncertainty with no concrete impact; minimal score of 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Any resurgence in COVID-19 could result in the imposition of new mandates and prolonged restrictive measures implemented in order to control the spread of the disease.

components.reason: Warns of renewed government restrictions that could hamper operations.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential for renewed lockdowns carries some risk but is still speculative; score 2.

evidence_list.snippet: The continued global spread of COVID-19 could adversely impact the Company’s operations, including, among other things, our manufacturing operations, supply chain, including third-party suppliers, sales and marketing and clinical trial operations.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple critical functions (manufacturing, supply chain, sales, clinical trials).
Frames impact as potentially adverse and global in scope.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Multi-function, enterprise-wide threat earns a high severity score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Any of these factors could adversely affect the Company’s business, financial results, and global economic conditions generally.

components.reason: Connects COVID-related factors to overall business and macro-economic harm.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad but generic statement of harm; limited incremental insight, so score 2.

evidence_list.snippet: We also face uncertainties related to our COVID-19 vaccine, including uncertainties related to the risk that our continued development programs may not be successful, commercially viable or receive approval from regulatory authorities; risks associated with clinical trial and real-world data, including further analyses of its efficacy, safety and durability; the risk that data are subject to differing interpretations and assessments, including during the peer review/publication process, in the scientific community generally, and by national immunization technical advisory groups (NITAGs) and regulatory authorities; disruptions in the relationships between us, our third-party suppliers and external manufacturers; the risk that other companies may produce superior or competitive products; the risk that demand for any products we may develop may no longer exist; risks related to the availability of raw materials to manufacture any such products; the risk that we may not be able to recoup costs associated with our R&D and manufacturing efforts and risks associated with any changes in the way we approach or provide additional research funding for potential drug development related to COVID-19; the risk that we may not be able to create or scale up manufacturing capacity on a timely basis, that we may continue to experience manufacturing delays once a manufacturing site is activated, or have access to logistics or supply channels commensurate with global demand for any potential approved vaccine or product candidate, which would negatively impact our ability to supply the estimated numbers of doses of our vaccine within the projected time periods indicated, and other challenges and risks associated with the pace of our vaccine development program; and pricing and access challenges for such products, including in the U.S.

components.reason: Lists multiple tangible risks (R&D failure, regulatory, competitive, supply chain, raw materials, manufacturing delays).
Specifically implicates third-party suppliers and logistics constraints.
Vaccine-specific; may not impact entire company equally.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive but vaccine-focused risk set; substantial but not enterprise-wide, score 5.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, to the extent the COVID-19 pandemic adversely affects our business and financial results, it may also have the effect of heightening many of the other risks described in this “Risk Factors” section and those incorporated by reference herein, including risks relating to the Company’s effective tax rate as a result of changes in consumption as well as changes in laws relating to supply of the Company’s products .

components.reason: States pandemic can amplify multiple pre-existing risk categories.
Provides no detail or quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recognises risk-multiplier effect but very general; low score 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Manufacturing disruptions can occur for many reasons including regulatory action, production quality deviations or safety issues, labor disputes, labor shortages, site-specific incidents (such as fires), natural disasters such as hurricanes and other severe weather events, raw material shortages, political unrest, terrorist attacks and epidemics or pandemics.

components.reason: Explicitly names epidemics/pandemics as potential causes of manufacturing disruption.
Statement is generic and bundled with many other causes.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic mention of pandemics within a broader disruption list; minimal incremental severity.
